method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with JSMO and Asian oncology societies (Yoshino et al.), ESMO Open 8(3):101558 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer' (published 24 May 2023), 22 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC10220270). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW 'eviQ metastatic colorectal cancer protocols (protocols, not guidelines): 1542 'FOLFOX6 (modified) and panitumumab' (v.8, review as required), 5001 'ipilimumab and nivolumab' (v.1, first approved 15 June 2026, review due 30 June 2027), 4111 'cetuximab and encorafenib' (v.4, review due 31 December 2027), 4394 'trifluridine/tipiracil and bevacizumab' (v.1, review due 30 June 2026) and 4552 'fruquintinib' (v.2, first approved 1 October 2025, review due 31 December 2026)' (retrieved 24 September 2026), 10 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that its content should not be hosted on external sites, and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright). Adaptations must cite the eviQ ID, version and URL. (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright page)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, five Australian eviQ treatment protocols (paraphrased and hash-anchored), for the regimen doses, eligibility, monitoring and pivotal-trial results that S1's stripped tables do not carry. The S2 source file concatenates https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1542, /p/5001, /p/4111, /p/4394 and /p/4552, each under a header line naming its URL. S1 claims and anchors are unchanged.

claims.claim: **Do not restrict HER2 amplification testing to RAS wild-type tumours**; test RAS-mutant disease too where resources and reimbursement allow, and if testing is not funded consider referral to a centre running trials.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with JSMO and Asian oncology societies (Yoshino et al.), ESMO Open 8(3):101558, 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer', published 24 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10220270/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Testing HER2 together with RAS, BRAF and dMMR/MSI in one pass saves tumour tissue.**
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with JSMO and Asian oncology societies (Yoshino et al.), ESMO Open 8(3):101558, 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer', published 24 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10220270/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **DPD testing (genotype or phenotype) may be considered before a fluoropyrimidine, depending on the population, and should be done after severe fluoropyrimidine toxicity.** The Asian panel softened ESMO's advice because DPD deficiency is rare in Asian patients (about 0.6% in one Japanese series).

claims.claim: **UGT1A1 genotyping before irinotecan** is advised if UGT1A1 deficiency is suspected (low conjugated bilirubin) or if a dose above 180 mg/m² per administration is planned; the variants raise the risk of severe neutropenia.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with JSMO and Asian oncology societies (Yoshino et al.), ESMO Open 8(3):101558, 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer', published 24 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10220270/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not deny resection or ablation just because first-line chemotherapy failed.** Reassess for resection once second-line treatment is working; intra-arterial chemotherapy can be a second-line route to response and liver resection.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with JSMO and Asian oncology societies (Yoshino et al.), ESMO Open 8(3):101558, 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer', published 24 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10220270/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Local treatment can be the primary or metastasis-directed treatment, or consolidation after systemic therapy.**
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with JSMO and Asian oncology societies (Yoshino et al.), ESMO Open 8(3):101558, 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer', published 24 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10220270/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intra-arterial options (TACE, TARE/SIRT, hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy)** may be used with non-curative intent.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Left-sided, RAS wild-type: anti-EGFR antibody plus doublet chemotherapy.** In a Japanese phase III trial, panitumumab with mFOLFOX6 gave longer overall survival, higher response and more R0 resections than bevacizumab with mFOLFOX6.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **FOLFOX6 (modified) with panitumumab, first line for RAS wild-type disease (eviQ):** every 14 days, panitumumab 6 mg/kg, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², calcium folinate 50 mg flat bolus and fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2,400 mg/m² by pump over 46 hours, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Consider stopping oxaliplatin after 6 cycles, and do not exceed 12; maintenance can continue if stable or responding.

claims.claim: **EGFR antibody and FOLFOX safety:** acneiform rash usually peaks in weeks 2 to 4 (moisturiser, sunscreen, consider early doxycycline and 1% hydrocortisone); check magnesium and calcium before each cycle and for up to 8 weeks after stopping; expect cold-triggered oxaliplatin neuropathy within 48 hours of a dose. DPYD genotyping has been MBS-listed since 1 November 2025.

At a median 47 months, median PFS was not reached with the combination versus 39.3 months with nivolumab alone (HR 0.62); response 71% v 58%; grade 3–4 treatment-related events 22% v 14%.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Encorafenib with cetuximab (eviQ):** BRAF V600E-mutant disease progressing after at least one line, ECOG 0 to 2, never given an EGFR antibody. Encorafenib 300 mg by mouth daily with cetuximab 400 mg/m² loading then 250 mg/m² weekly (500 mg/m² every 14 days is an alternative), continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity. In BEACON, median overall survival was 9.3 v 5.9 months (HR 0.61) and response 19.5% v 1.8%; adding binimetinib did not improve survival.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cetuximab anaphylaxis risk is higher with red-meat allergy, tick bites or alpha-gal IgE;** consider alpha-gal testing in people from tick-endemic areas. On encorafenib, do not start if QTc exceeds 500 ms, and send any visual disturbance promptly to an ophthalmologist (uveitis, serous retinopathy), withholding treatment until reviewed.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Trifluridine/tipiracil with bevacizumab (eviQ):** ECOG 0 to 1, once fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin and irinotecan regimens, a VEGF inhibitor and (for RAS wild-type tumours) an EGFR antibody have been used or are unsuitable. Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² twice daily (maximum 80 mg a dose) on days 1–5 and 8–12, with bevacizumab 5 mg/kg on days 1 and 15, every 28 days. Median overall survival was 10.8 v 7.5 months with trifluridine/tipiracil alone (HR 0.61).

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fruquintinib (eviQ):** ECOG 0 to 1, once fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin and irinotecan regimens, a VEGF inhibitor and, where suitable, an EGFR antibody have been given. 5 mg by mouth once daily, 3 weeks on then 1 week off. Avoid with significant cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled hypertension or thromboembolism in the past 6 months; check blood pressure weekly for the first month then monthly, and LFTs every 2 weeks for 2 months. Median overall survival was 7.4 v 4.8 months with placebo (HR 0.66).
